subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: Should OpenClaw add a server-controlled per-agent foreground command-lane config surface for inbound agent runs, and what exact config/safety contract should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates public scheduler/config semantics and must coordinate with adjacent hook, subagent, browser, and per-channel lane proposals.

options.title: Design Server-Controlled Per-Agent Lanes
options.body: Add a trusted config-driven foreground lane contract that derives lanes from agent config, preserves a global safety cap, rejects request-controlled arbitrary lanes, and documents upgrade behavior.

options.title: Unify Under A Scheduler RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers design one lane/concurrency model covering foreground, hook, subagent, browser, and channel-specific work.

options.title: Decline Core Lane Config
options.body: Keep the shared main lane as the only foreground core contract and document separate gateway deployments or narrower plugin/hook surfaces for isolation.

recommendation.title: Design Server-Controlled Per-Agent Lanes
recommendation.body: Add a trusted config-driven foreground lane contract that derives lanes from agent config, preserves a global safety cap, rejects request-controlled arbitrary lanes, and documents upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The related reviews and issue comments route the public scheduler/config decision through this contributor's recent gateway lane and config history.
